newsitem.title: USA: Carnival Air Lines chairman/CEO Wertheim resigns.
newsitem.headline: Carnival Air Lines chairman/CEO Wertheim resigns.

text.p: Carnival Air Lines, which has a pending agreement to be acquired by Pan Am Corp, said Thursday that its chairman and chief executive officer, Reuven Wertheim, has resigned.
The airline's president, Ray Vecci, will assume Wertheim's responsibilities, the company said.

Wertheim, a 35-year veteran of the airline industry, plans to launch a consulting firm under the name Commercial Aviation Associates Inc and additionally will become a shareholder of and consultant to Pan Am, it said.
Wertheim co-founded Carnival Air Lines in 1988 with cruise pioneer Micky Arison, who is chairman and chief executive of Carnival Corp.

Privately-held Carnival Air, which is not part of Carnival Corp, started business with one plane and 35 employees. Today it has 1,600 employees, 27 jets and service to nearly 20 destinations in the Northeast, Florida, California and the Caribbean.
